paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits for Real-Time Strategy Games

unmapped: Macro-arms are tuples of values of n variables, variable X_i taking K_i values (product action space), with a legality function L restricting which macro-arms are allowed
Only the reward of the whole macro-arm is observed (full-bandit feedback on a combinatorial action); the reward is an arbitrary unknown function of the macro-arm (no linearity assumed)
settings.definition_quote: A set of $n$ variables $X = \{X_1, ..., X_n\}$, where variable $X_i$ can take $K_i$ different values ... each of these combinations $V \in \mathcal{X}$ is called a {\em macro-arm}. An unknown reward distribution $\mu : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ over each macro-arm. A function $L : \mathcal{X} \to \{true,false\}$ that determines which macro-arms are legal.

unmapped: Macro-arms are tuples of values of n variables, variable X_i taking K_i values (product action space), with a legality function L restricting which macro-arms are allowed
Only the reward of the whole macro-arm is observed (full-bandit feedback on a combinatorial action); the reward is an arbitrary unknown function of the macro-arm
settings.definition_quote: Simple regret: after $T$ iterations, the simple regret is the difference between $\mu^*$ and the reward obtained by the macro-arm believed to be the best at iteration $T$: $r_T = \mu^* - \mu(V_T^{best})$

algorithms.name: epsilon-greedy Naive Sampling NS(eps_0, eps_l, eps_g)
Two-phase Naive Sampling NS(k, eps_0^1, eps_l^1, eps_g^1, eps_0^2, eps_l^2, eps_g^2)

symbols.p_opt: asymptotic probability of selecting an optimal macro-arm, p^* >= (1-eps_0)(1-eps_g)
symbols.D_avg: expected difference in expected reward between an optimal macro-arm and a (uniformly averaged) non-optimal legal macro-arm

tuning: pi_0, pi_l, pi_g are epsilon-greedy with parameters eps_0, eps_l, eps_g

source.label: ens-cumulative-proposition
source.quote: The {\em cumulative regret} of NS($\epsilon_0$,$\epsilon_l$,$\epsilon_g$) grows linearly as $R_T = O((1 - p^*) D T)$, where $T$ is the number of iterations, $D$ is the expected difference in expected reward between an optimal macro-arm and a non-optimal macro-arm, and $p^* \geq (1 - \epsilon_0)(1 - \epsilon_g)$ is the probability of selecting an optimal arm when $T \to \infty$

results.notes: Heuristic asymptotic argument (instantaneous regret ≈ (1-p*)D). Paper's D renamed D_avg to avoid clash with delay symbol. Linear regret statement.

symbols.D_avg: expected difference in expected reward between an optimal macro-arm and a non-optimal macro-arm
symbols.d_gap: minimum difference in reward between an optimal macro-arm and a non-optimal macro-arm
symbols.p_sel: p_i >= eps_0 prod_j eps_l/K_j + (1-eps_0) eps_g/N, lower bound on the per-round probability of selecting a given suboptimal macro-arm (N = number of legal macro-arms)

conditions: proof assumes eps_0 <= 0.5, eps_g <= 0.5, eps_l <= 0.5 and N >> 2
tuning: epsilon-greedy pi_0, pi_l, pi_g with parameters eps_0, eps_l, eps_g

source.label: ens-simple-proposition
source.quote: The {\em simple regret} of NS($\epsilon_0$,$\epsilon_l$,$\epsilon_g$) decreases at an exponential rate as $r_T = O(D e^{-2d^2 T p_i})$, where $p_i \geq \epsilon_0 \Pi_{j = 1...n}\frac{\epsilon_l}{K_j} + (1-\epsilon_0)\frac{\epsilon_g}{N}$, $D$ is as in Proposition~\ref{ens-cumulative-proposition}, and $d$ is the minimum difference in reward between an optimal macro-arm and a non-optimal macro-arm

results.notes: Heuristic proof via Hoeffding (implicitly assumes rewards in a unit range) using expected sample counts. Paper's d renamed d_gap to avoid clash with dimension.

symbols.eps_0: probability of choosing explore in NS

tuning: epsilon-greedy NS with parameters eps_0, eps_l, eps_g

source.label: prop:2phase-explore
source.quote: In a CMAB with $n$ variables, the probability that after $t$ iterations using a NS$(\epsilon_0, \epsilon_l, \epsilon_g)$ sampling strategy an optimal macro-arm $V^*$ has not been explored at least once, decreases exponentially as a function of $t$, and is at most $(1-p)^{t\epsilon_0}$, where $p = \prod_{i = 1 ... n} \left(\epsilon_l/K_i\right)$

results.notes: Bound on probability the optimal macro-arm is never explored after t=T iterations; proof uses the expected number of exploration rounds t*eps_0 as if deterministic.

symbols.eps_g: global-MAB epsilon in the second phase
symbols.d_gap: difference between the best non-optimal macro-arm and an optimal macro-arm
symbols.D_avg: difference between an optimal macro-arm and a random macro-arm
symbols.k_phase: length k of the first phase

tuning: second-phase eps_0^2 = 0 (the proposition writes the second-phase local parameter as 0)
first phase lasts a constant number k of iterations

source.label: prop:2phase-cumulative
source.quote: The {\em cumulative regret} of NS($k,\epsilon_0^1,\epsilon_l^1,\epsilon_g^1, \epsilon_0^2, 0, \epsilon_g^2$) when $k$ is a constant grows linearly when $T \gg k$: $$R_T = O\left(t\left[ (1 -\epsilon_g - q_k + \epsilon_g q_k)d + \epsilon_g D \right]\right)$$ where $q_k = 1 - (1-p)^{k\epsilon_0^1}$, and $p = \prod_{i = 1 ... n} \left(\epsilon_l^1/K_i\right)$.

results.notes: Paper writes t for the horizon in the bound; mapped to T. Text says the case considered is eps_0^2 = 0 though the tuple puts 0 in the eps_l^2 position; inconsistent notation. Heuristic asymptotic analysis.

bound.regime: k constant, T >> k (limit T -> infinity)

symbols.d_gap: difference between the best non-optimal macro-arm and an optimal macro-arm

conditions: applies only to the specific algorithm two-phase NS(k, eps_0^1, eps_l^1, eps_g^1, eps_0^2, 0, eps_g^2) with constant first-phase length k

source.label: prop:2phase-simple
source.quote: The {\em simple regret} of NS($k,\epsilon_0^1,\epsilon_l^1,\epsilon_g^1, \epsilon_0^2, 0, \epsilon_g^2$) when $k$ is a constant and $T \gg k$ is lower bounded by $(1-q_k)d$, where $q_k = 1 - (1-p)^{k\epsilon_0^1}$, and $d$ is difference between the best non-optimal macro-arm and an optimal macro-arm.

results.notes: Algorithm-specific lower bound showing non-vanishing simple regret; derived as the T->infinity limit of an approximate expression.
